title: Another emerging job: the agent orchestrator
oneliner: Enterprises now run digital agents inside DevOps and operations teams, and they need a human in the loop to manage them - that role is the agent orchestrator.
says: A new role is emerging: the agent orchestrator. Enterprises are deploying digital agents that help operations teams - DevOps, DevSecOps - automate tasks intelligently, saving money and raising efficiency. But you cannot rely on these agents completely; a human must manage them. That human-in-the-loop role is the agent orchestrator, and it is showing up in the job market.
explained: Think of it as the management layer for a workforce that is partly software. Agents drift, fail, misread situations, and occasionally act confidently on bad inputs. The orchestrator supervises: approving consequential actions, catching failures, tuning which tasks agents may do alone, and owning the outcome when automation misfires.

This is the org-chart version of a theme that runs through the whole archive - enterprises do not buy autonomy, they buy supervised autonomy. The governance reels say why (accountability), the evaluation episode in Season 2 says how you measure whether agents deserve more leash, and this reel says who holds the leash day to day.
takeaway: Agent adoption creates management jobs, not just engineering jobs: supervising, approving, and tuning agent workforces is becoming a titled role.
